To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
flooding regimes and soil properties are important predictors of Neotropical dry forest diversity, composition, and structure.

(1) tree species richness is higher in dry forests never subjected to flooding than in those flooded annually; (2) dry forests flooded annually tend to be dominated by multi-stemmed species; and (3) soil chemical attributes, not flooding regime, affect above ground biomass.
